135905.text: Three different subtypes of the cluster event resource "Pod" are being added: "AssignedPod", "UnscheduledPod", "TargetPod". Plugins can and are expected to register to specific pod events for better performance.
135905.markdown: Three different subtypes of the cluster event resource "Pod" are being added: "AssignedPod", "UnscheduledPod", "TargetPod". Plugins can and are expected to register to specific pod events for better performance. ([#135905](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135905), [@iomarsayed](https://github.com/iomarsayed)) [SIG Node, Scheduling, Storage and Testing]
135905.author: iomarsayed
135905.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Right now, if a plugin is subscribed to a cluster pod event, and such events happen, plugin will execute its corresponding queuing hint function, but it may be useless. resulting in performance loss.

Example Scenario:
When a pod that is part of a gang is added, an event "Pod/Add" happen (to possibly requeue unschedulable other gang pods to complete the gang), and while many plugins are registered to it, only one single plugin benefits from this exact case: **GangScheduling** plugin.

Solution:
We Refine cluster events, by splitting the pod resource into three different types: "AssignedPod", "UnscheduledPod" and "TargetPod". Now we can have more specific cluster events, and plugins subscribe to such events instead.
Also most of plugin queuing hint functions are updated to be specific according to pod resource type.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes #135528

None

```release-note
Three different subtypes of the cluster event resource "Pod" are being added: "AssignedPod", "UnscheduledPod", "TargetPod". Plugins can and are expected to register to specific pod events for better performance.
```

136271.markdown: Removed the unused `PodStatusResult` type from the Kubernetes API. This type had no REST endpoint and has been unused since 2015. 136271.author: adityasharmawork
136271.pr_body:
The PodStatusResult type in pkg/apis/core is defined but not referenced anywhere.

  #### What type of PR is this?

  /kind cleanup
  /kind api-change

  #### What this PR does / why we need it:

  This PR removes the unused `PodStatusResult` type from the Kubernetes API.

  **Background:**
  - `PodStatusResult` was introduced in January 2015 ([PR #3565](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/3565)) as a wrapper type for encoding/decoding pod status returned by kubelet's `/podInfo` endpoint
  - Just 4 months later (May 2015), the `/podInfo` endpoint was removed when kubelet architecture changed to push status updates directly to the API server
  - The type has been completely unused for over 10 years
  - It was never exposed via any REST API endpoint to users

  **Why remove it:**
  - The type is vestigial and serves no purpose
  - Any change to Pod status fields (like adding new fields) causes unnecessary test fixture churn for this unused type (see [#135196](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135196))
  - Removing it reduces maintenance burden and codebase complexity

  **Changes:**
  - Removed `PodStatusResult` struct from `pkg/apis/core/types.go` and `staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go`
  - Removed type registration from both internal and versioned scheme
  - Deleted all test fixtures for `core.v1.PodStatusResult`
  - Updated integration tests that referenced this type

  #### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

  Fixes #136250

  #### Special notes for your reviewer:

  This type was never user-facing - it had no REST endpoint and was only used internally for kubelet-to-apiserver communication via an endpoint that was removed in 2015. Direct removal is appropriate since:
  1. No deprecation period is needed for types that were never exposed to users
  2. There are no external consumers that could be affected
  3. The type has been unused for 10+ years

  The original PR #3565 comment from @bgrant0607: "This is an intermediate state in the path towards just exposing the pod API in Kubelet" - that path was completed long ago.

  #### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Removed the unused `PodStatusResult` type from the Kubernetes API. This type had no REST endpoint and has been unused since 2015.
```

  N/A

137767.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Adds Prometheus metrics for Windows kube-proxy (winkernel) load balancer
operation failures. Previously, the winkernel proxier had no metrics for LB
failures, making it difficult to monitor and diagnose issues in production
Windows clusters.

This PR introduces three new `ALPHA` stability counter metrics:

- `kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_create_failures_total` - tracks LB creation failures
- `kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_update_failures_total` - tracks LB update failures
- `kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_winkernel_lb_delete_failures_total` - tracks LB deletion failures

Each metric has three labels for fine-grained observability:

- `ip_family` - `IPv4` or `IPv6`
- `lb_type` - `clusterip`, `nodeport`, `externalip`, `ingressip`, or `healthcheck`
- `error`  - `network_not_found`, `port_already_exists`, `not_implemented`, `invalid_ip`, or `other`

The maximum cardinality per metric is 50 (2 × 5 × 5), but in practice is much
lower since a proxier instance uses a single IP family and most error/lb_type
combinations never fire.

**Implementation details:**

- Defines type-safe `loadBalancerType` and `lbErrorType` string typedefs with constants
- Adds a `classifyLBError` function that maps HCN/HNS errors to a finite set of error categories using the hcn package's error classification helpers
- Changes `mapStaleLoadbalancers` from `map[string]bool` to `map[string]loadBalancerType` to preserve the LB type through stale LB cleanup retries
- Threads `lbType` through `deleteExistingLoadBalancer`, `deleteLoadBalancer`, `deleteLoadBalancerPolicy`, and `cleanupAllPolicies`
- Emits metrics at all 8 failure sites (3 create, 3 update, 2 delete paths)
- Registers the new metrics under `ProxyModeKernelspace` in `RegisterMetrics`

138000.text: Fixed stale remote HNS endpoint cleanup on Windows when a pod IP is reused across nodes in L2Bridge networks, preventing DNS timeouts caused by traffic being routed to the wrong node.
138000.markdown: Fixed stale remote HNS endpoint cleanup on Windows when a pod IP is reused across nodes in L2Bridge networks, preventing DNS timeouts caused by traffic being routed to the wrong node. ([#138000](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138000), [@princepereira](https://github.com/princepereira)) [SIG Network and Windows]
138000.author: princepereira
138000.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

**Handling Stale Remote Endpoints When Local and Remote Endpoints Share the Same IP (getAllEndpointsByNetwork)**

On Windows Server 2019 and Windows Server 2022, within an L2Bridge network configuration, all pods across cluster nodes typically share the same pod subnet.

In scenarios where the subnet range is limited, or even when larger ranges are heavily utilized, IP address reuse can occur. For example, when a pod assigned an IP address (e.g., 10.0.0.1) is deleted, that IP may later be reassigned to a new pod on a different node immediately. In such cases, the CNI creates a new local endpoint for the reused IP.

However, the corresponding remote endpoint associated with the previously deleted pod may not yet have been cleaned up, as it could still be awaiting deletion signals. Because the IP is already reassigned locally, KubeProxy may inadvertently increase the reference count of the stale remote endpoint and delay its removal. This can result in both a local and a remote endpoint coexisting with the same IP address in HNS.

This duplication can lead to unintended behavior. For instance, when a pod using the reused IP attempts DNS resolution, traffic is load-balanced at the host port (particularly in non-DSR mode). After DNAT, the VFP rule may select the MAC address of the remote endpoint instead of the local pod. Since subsequent VFP processing interprets this as traffic destined for a remote endpoint, packets may be encapsulated and routed to an incorrect node rather than the appropriate DNS pod. This can ultimately cause DNS timeouts.

To address this issue, the fix prioritizes local endpoints. When a local endpoint is detected for an IP that also has a remote endpoint, the remote endpoint is marked for deletion and replaced by the local one. Additionally, any stale remote endpoints with duplicate IP addresses are systematically cleaned up using deleteAllRemoteEndpointsWithDupIP at the end of each syncProxyRules() cycle.

Fixes #137381

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When `checkAndDecrement` returns a `Forbidden` error due to negative `DisruptionsAllowed` or an oversized `DisruptedPods` map, clients had no programmatic way to distinguish these from other `Forbidden` errors without string-matching on the message.

- `DisruptionBudgetNegativeAllowedDisruptions` — for the `DisruptionsAllowed < 0` case

Clients can now use `errors.HasStatusCause(err, policyv1.DisruptionBudgetNegativeAllowedDisruptions)` for reliable, typed, machine-readable error discrimination, no message parsing needed.

The two new `CauseType` constants follow the same naming convention and placement as the existing `DisruptionBudgetCause` constant in `staging/src/k8s.io/api/policy/v1/types.go`. No codegen changes were required since `CauseType` is a `string` alias.

138367.text: Fixed a bug where pods with multiple subPath volume mounts on Windows would get stuck in Terminating state because file handles from subPath preparation were leaked, preventing volume cleanup.
138367.markdown: Fixed a bug where pods with multiple subPath volume mounts on Windows would get stuck in Terminating state because file handles from subPath preparation were leaked, preventing volume cleanup. 138367.author: timmy-wright
138367.pr_body:
## What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

## What this PR does / why we need it
Fixes a file handle leak in `makeMounts()` that causes emptyDir volumes to fail cleanup on Windows, leaving pods stuck in Terminating state after deletion.

In `makeMounts()`, a single `cleanupAction` variable was overwritten each time `PrepareSafeSubpath()` was called in the volume mount loop. On Windows, `PrepareSafeSubpath` acquires file handles via `syscall.CreateFile` (in `lockAndCheckSubPath` → `lockPath`) to prevent symlink race attacks. Because only the last mount's cleanup function was returned to the caller (`kuberuntime_container.go:255: defer cleanupAction()`), all prior handles leaked permanently. This prevented `os.RemoveAll` from deleting the emptyDir volume directory during pod teardown.

Linux is unaffected because its `PrepareSafeSubpath` uses bind mounts and always returns `cleanupAction = nil`.

## How does this fix it?
Replaces the single `cleanupAction` variable with a `[]func{}` slice accumulator. Each call to `PrepareSafeSubpath` appends its cleanup to the slice, and the composite `cleanupAction` closure invokes all of them when called.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/112630

## Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Fixed a bug where pods with multiple subPath volume mounts on Windows would get stuck in Terminating state because file handles from subPath preparation were leaked, preventing volume cleanup.
```

## Testing
- **Unit test**: `TestMakemountsSubpathCleanupAccumulation` with 5 table-driven cases covering multi-mount cleanup accumulation, single mount, no subpaths, and error paths (verifying earlier cleanups still fire when a later mount fails)
- **E2e test**: Windows-specific test that creates a pod with 3 subPath mounts from a ConfigMap and verifies it terminates cleanly after deletion

/sig node
/sig windows
/area kubelet

`containerEphemeralStorageLimitEviction()` only iterates `pod.Spec.Containers` when building the per-container ephemeral-storage threshold map. This PR adds iteration over `pod.Spec.InitContainers` for restartable init containers when building the threshold map, so the existing per-container comparison covers them.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

138771.text: Optimized CEL admission policy evaluation by adopting a lazy zero-allocation reflection-based utility for object traversal, significantly reducing CPU usage and garbage collection overhead during request processing.
138771.markdown: Optimized CEL admission policy evaluation by adopting a lazy zero-allocation reflection-based utility for object traversal, significantly reducing CPU usage and garbage collection overhead during request processing. ([#138771](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138771), [@lalitc375](https://github.com/lalitc375)) [SIG API Machinery, Architecture, Auth, CLI, Cloud Provider, Cluster Lifecycle, Network, Node, Scheduling and Storage]
138771.author: lalitc375
138771.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR optimizes the CEL admission policy evaluation pipeline to significantly reduce CPU usage and garbage collection pressure.

Previously, the CEL admission environment prepared variables like `object` and `oldObject` by passing them through `convertObjectToUnstructured`. This relied heavily on generic JSON reflection loops and allocations, making it very expensive for high-throughput admission controllers.

This PR introduces `UnstructuredReflectToVal`, a zero-allocation reflection-based utility that lazily traverses structured Go objects to construct CEL `ref.Val` representations. This mimics standard unstructured conversion while bypassing expensive full-map allocation and serializer lookups.

Key Changes:
1. **Lazy Conversion Pipeline**: Integrates `UnstructuredReflectToVal` into the `VersionedAttributes` lazy conversion pipeline (`LazyObject.CELValue`) to optimize admission variable preparation.
2. **Robust Nil-Handling**: Implements robust pointer, interface, map, and slice nil-handling to map Go nil values to JSON-equivalent `NullValue` objects. 
3. **Custom Marshaling**: Adds custom marshaling resolution for both pointer and value receiver implementations (`json.Marshaler` / `ToUnstructured`), including dynamically wrapper-addressing struct value fields.
4. **Structural Field Alignment**: Aligns structural field selection in `lookupField` to correctly return `NullValue` (instead of omitting) for non-omitempty nil fields.
5. **Equivalence Testing**: Introduces a comprehensive equivalence test suite (`converter_equivalence_test.go`) verifying absolute behavioral alignment with the Kubernetes `runtime.DefaultUnstructuredConverter.ToUnstructured` serialization.



#### Benchmark Results:
I've run benchmarks comparing the old and new setup. You can view the full benchmark files and results in this [GitHub Gist](https://gist.github.com/lalitc375/d895a5ebfc7292bb42f560b55d677ee6).

**Highlights:**
- `BenchmarkRealisticPod_Setup`: **~96% reduction in ns/op** (53320 ns -> 2098 ns) and significant drop in allocations (216 -> 2 allocs/op).
- `BenchmarkRealisticNestedField_MutliplePolicies (accessing same field in the all policies)`: **~86% reduction in ns/op** (379.6 ns -> 50.07 ns) and zero allocations.
- `BenchmarkVAPSEvaluation_9Policies ( random fields in all policies)`: Performance improved from 89006 ns/op to 58160 ns/op with a 63% reduction in allocs (527 -> 191).

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Part of #131520

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
Integration tests under `test/integration/apiserver/cel/...` have been verified to pass locally. The new `converter_equivalence_test.go` suite guarantees behavioral parity with the existing standard unstructured conversion across nested/inlined structs, omitempty tags, and custom marshaler implementations.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Optimized CEL admission policy evaluation by adopting a lazy zero-allocation reflection-based utility for object traversal, significantly reducing CPU usage and garbage collection overhead during request processing.
```

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When a subpath mount point is corrupted (e.g. stale NFS file handle), kubelet cannot recover from it during container restart and the pod gets stuck in `CreateContainerConfigError`. Instead, we can try to recover by unmounting the corrupted mount and remounting when kubelet is preparing the subpath.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

I've verified the patch and compared old and new versions:

## Setup

Pod `nfs-stale-test` mounts an NFS PVC with `subPathExpr: $(DIAGNOSTICS_SUBPATH)`.  
Pod `nfs-helper` mounts the same PVC at `/mnt/nfs` (raw, no subPath).  
Marker data written: `CRITICAL_DATA` to `/var/app/diagnostics/marker.txt`.

**Inode replacement** (from helper pod) invalidates the test pod's NFS4 file handle while preserving the directory and data:

```bash
kubectl exec nfs-helper -- sh -c '
  mv /mnt/nfs/nfs-stale-test /mnt/nfs/nfs-stale-test.bak;
  mkdir /mnt/nfs/nfs-stale-test;
  cp -a /mnt/nfs/nfs-stale-test.bak/* /mnt/nfs/nfs-stale-test/;
  rm -rf /mnt/nfs/nfs-stale-test.bak'
```

After this, the test pod returns `Stale file handle` but the helper pod can still read all data. Then the container is killed via `crictl stop`.

---

## BEFORE FIX

```
$ kubectl get pod nfs-stale-test
NAME             READY   STATUS                       RESTARTS   AGE
nfs-stale-test   0/1     CreateContainerConfigError   0          67s
```

```json
{"waiting":{"message":"failed to prepare subPath for volumeMount \"data\" of container \"main\"","reason":"CreateContainerConfigError"}}
```

**Kubelet log:**
```
E0507 kubelet_pods.go:371] "Failed to prepare subPath for volumeMount of the container"
  containerName="main" volumeMountName="data"
E0507 pod_workers.go:1324] "Error syncing pod, skipping"
  err="failed to \"StartContainer\" for \"main\" with CreateContainerConfigError"
```

Pod is **permanently stuck**. Restart count stays at 0. Requires manual intervention (pod deletion or host-level `umount`).

---

## AFTER FIX

```
$ kubectl get pod nfs-stale-test
NAME             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS      AGE
nfs-stale-test   1/1     Running   1 (15s ago)   46s
```

**Kubelet log:**
```
W0507 subpath_linux.go:104] Detected corrupted mount at /var/lib/kubelet/pods/53369a11-5f1e-412e-9d32-bd229039d133/volume-subpaths/nfs-test-pv/main/0 (error: lstat /var/lib/kubelet/pods/53369a11-5f1e-412e-9d32-bd229039d133/volume-subpaths/nfs-test-pv/main/0: stale file handle), unmounting
```

Pod **self-recovers**. Container restarts with all data intact:

```
$ kubectl exec nfs-stale-test -- cat /var/app/diagnostics/marker.txt
CRITICAL_DATA_PATCHED_TEST
```

138885.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When handling a ResourceClaim request with `allocationMode: All`, the structured DRA allocator precomputes all matching devices. That code path did not store the source pool in the `deviceWithID` candidate.

If one of those devices consumed shared counters, `checkAvailableCounters` dereferenced the missing pool and kube-scheduler panicked while filtering the Pod.

This PR sets the pool for `AllocationModeAll` device candidates in the stable, incubating, and experimental allocator variants, and adds a shared regression test for `AllocationModeAll` with consumed counters.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #138882

The new regression test fails with the original nil pointer panic if the `pool: pool` assignment is removed from the `AllocationModeAll` candidate construction path.

138951.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig scheduling

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`ImageLocality` already includes image volumes when calculating the raw image score, but `calculatePriority` only used the number of init containers and regular containers to derive the max score threshold.

As a result, image volumes contributed to `imageScores`, but did not contribute to the image count used for the threshold.

This PR makes `sumImageScores` return both the raw image score and the image source count, so the raw score and max threshold are based on the same image sources:

- regular containers
- init containers
- image volumes

This keeps ImageVolume scoring consistent with regular container image scoring.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Addresses #138952

No


139006.pr_body:
## What type of PR is this?
/kind cleanup
/kind flake

## What this PR does / why we need it

These tests have race conditions where they assume immediate state visibility after a pod transitions to `Running`. The current code works on fast runtimes but is fundamentally racy: kubelet log streaming, log file flushing, and container status updates are eventually consistent, not synchronous.

Switching to `gomega.Eventually` polling makes the tests deterministic. The success path on fast runtimes is unchanged (polling succeeds on first attempt), but the tests now correctly handle scenarios where state takes a moment to propagate. This benefits any environment where containers may take longer to start (VM-isolated runtimes such as Kata, gVisor, and Windows Hyper-V; overloaded CI VMs; shared multi-tenant clusters).

### Changes

- **`ephemeral_containers.go`** (both `should be added` and `should update` tests): the `polo` log-content check is polled via `gomega.Eventually` with `f.Timeouts.PodStartShort`. The container may report Running before its first stdout has been flushed.

- **`lifecycle_hook.go`** (`ignore terminated container`): use `f.Timeouts.PodDelete` instead of `gracePeriod*time.Second` for the termination wait. The actual correctness check (container's intrinsic `StartedAt`/`FinishedAt` < `sleepSeconds`) is unchanged and unaffected by how long we waited.

- **`pods.go`** (`retrieving logs from the container over websockets`): poll the websocket open and read via `gomega.Eventually`. The container can be reported Running before its first stdout line has been flushed, so opening the websocket immediately may return an empty or partial buffer.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

None — observed as recurring flakes in capz-windows-master-hyperv CI but the underlying races affect any sufficiently slow environment.

## Special notes for your reviewer

These are pure robustness improvements:
- No test semantics change — same things are validated
- No happy-path slowdown — polling succeeds on first attempt when state is already there
- No new dependencies, no new test infrastructure

## Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```
elease-note
NONE
```

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR is the second step of splitting the work originally proposed in #138883.

It evolves the shared `apiserver_storage_list_*` metrics to carry the labels

- the watch cache path records the same metric family with `storage="watchcache"`

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

A pod can become stuck in unschedulable queue in the following sequence:

1. While the preemptor pod is waiting for preemption, change the cluster in a way that will re-queue the pod. The DefaultPreemption's PreEnqueue will return Unschedulable which will gate the pod
2. The relevant plugins don't return fwk.Queue hint once the victim pods are deleted. This can happen if there's a bug in queue hint implementation (e.g. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139161)

The fix is to make gated pods react to flushes, providing a failsafe. Alternatively, we could ungate the preemptor pod once the preemption completes.

> When two pods in a PodGroup share a ResourceClaim, the dra scheduler plugin reuses the in-memory `pendingAllocation` created during the `Reserve` phase of the first pod (`pod0`). However, during `PreFilter` when reusing `pendingAllocation`

> 
> , `s.informationsForClaim[index].availableOnNodes` is never set. As a result, during the `Filter` phase
> 
> https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a0b6070d29d7408c37ea09c8dbb46c91cb9e7c65/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/dynamicresources/dynamicresources.go#L763
> 
> , `availableOnNodes` evaluates to `nil`, skipping node selector validation for subsequent pods (`pod1`).
> This allows `pod1` to be successfully scheduled onto a node (`worker-1`) even if the allocated device physically resides on a different node (`worker-0`).

I think the reason that `availableOnNodes` was omitted was because #137647 didn't need it but it should have been added in #137897.

140131.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

  /kind cleanup

  #### What this PR does / why we need it:

  This PR avoids reporting `Incorrect event registration` for scheduler pod event resources like `AssignedPod`, `UnscheduledPod`, and `TargetPod`.

  These resources are logical pod event resources. The scheduler already registers the pod informer, and these events are emitted from pod add/update/delete handling. They should not
  try to register another informer by GVK parsing.

  Without this change, scheduler integration tests can keep printing logs like:

  ```text
  UnhandledError: Incorrect event registration gvk=<framework.EventResource>: AssignedPod
  UnhandledError: Incorrect event registration gvk=<framework.EventResource>: UnscheduledPod
  UnhandledError: Incorrect event registration gvk=<framework.EventResource>: TargetPod
```
  This PR makes these pod event resources use the existing pod informer path, and adds a test to cover this behavior.

140201.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This fixes a bug where slight differences in the typed and unstructured representation of objects, such as quantity being a string vs. being a typed object, would be observable to CEL expressions *only* when a informer cache miss resulted in a direct object lookup using the dynamic client.

We expect cache hits for the informer to be more common, so expectation is that developers will have authored CEL expressions against the cache hit behavior. For this reason, and because the typed representation used by infromers is generally preferred, we fix this by converting to the cache miss get responses to the structured type.

Because this code path is uncommon, no performance impact is expected.

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

After PodGroup Pods have passed the scheduling cycle, the binding cycle asynchronously invokes the Reserve and PreBind phases of the DynamicResources plugin. When a shared ResourceClaim is first allocated, other Pods in the group may have yet to reach the Reserve phase. If an in-flight allocation is recorded in Reserve for a claim that is already allocated, later removing that in-flight allocation results in `Restore`-ing the claim in the assume cache to an old version that may be unallocated. If the restored claim is unallocated, then the scheduler continuously falls into a loop:

- Claim in AssumeCache is unallocated
- Pending allocation is recorded
- API GET in PreBind yields the allocated claim
- "claim got allocated elsewhere" error

This change cuts off that cycle by verifying that claims are actually unallocated in the Reserve phase before recording an in-flight allocation.
